answer: Proposal: each ID/day serving harbor logs, trellis telemetry or velvet inventory binds a secure chip's certified, nonexportable key. The registry verifies maker certificates and fresh signed reads, allowing one ID per chip serial per day; failure denies listing. Chips are reusable capital; rental fees recur; no stake. Ten IDs need ten chips despite shared hosts or parallel signing. This assumes honest one-serial-per-chip issuance and intact key isolation; cheap chips weaken deterrence, and signatures do not prove feed accuracy.
